To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the finite-volume effects in SU(N) gauge theory are small for N≥3, and they become smaller as N is taken large.

(1) finite-volume effects on glueballs are surprisingly small in SU(N) gauge theory with N≥3, (2) the finite-volume spectrum of SU(N>4) gauge theories is dominated by torelons, (3) torelons mix with glueballs in SU(N≤6) gauge theory, (4) finite-volume effects are smaller in larger SU(N) gauge groups.
(1) the spectrum of SU(3) glueballs has been computed with high accuracy in finite volume, and that (2) finite-volume corrections to SU(6) glueballs are very small.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a systematic study of the spatial-volume dependence in the spectrum of 3+1-dimensional gauge theories, in the continuum limit and in the planar approximation, with the aim of finding a systematic expansion parameter for finite-volume corrections.
the study of SU(N) lattice gauge theory in finite volume and with the extraction of the glueball spectrum from the numerical results.
the study of the spectrum of the Yang-Mills field in the pure-gauge theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectrum of large-N gauge theories is remarkably insensitive to finite-volume corrections.
SU(N) gauge theory is a good candidate for a lattice theory with a smooth continuum limit.
, for all practical purposes, the glueball spectrum of pure gauge theories can be considered to be independent of the spatial volume, at least down L=1.2fm, and possibly even down to L=1fm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
finite volume is not a serious problem for the glueball spectrum of SU(3), even at the lowest-lying levels.
the SU(N) gauge theory spectrum is remarkably stable against spatial volume changes, at least down the L=0.8fm.
the spectrum of SU(N), N ≤ 6, in the large volume limit is well approximated in the planar large-N limit.
The main takeaway from our work is that
finite-volume effects in the SU(N) glueball spectrum become negligible for large N and large enough spatial volumes.
the glueballs are already quite stable in small volume, and the glueball spectrum in the continuum is likely to be very close to that of the large-volume lattice.
the spectrum of SU(N > 3) gauge theories is already very well approximated by the infinite-volume theory at spatial sizes L ≳ 1fm, which is much smaller than the string tension.
